title: Orbit document extraction: experiment log
scoring: Every field a page wants is one point: a right answer scores 1, a wrong answer and a blank both score 0 (owner, 2026-09-12 — weeding out wrong answers is its own job, not something to bend every measurement around). The 24 tuning pages are for steering; the 12 hold-out pages were never tuned on and are the judge. Runs before 2026-09-12 were scored the old way, where a wrong answer also lost a point, and are marked "old scoring": their numbers cannot be compared with the ones after.

corpora.holdout-12: The 12 hold-out pages, never read by an agent (extraction-holdout-corpus*.ts)
corpora.fullpage-6: The six full-page documents added on 2026-09-11 (#981), now part of the 24

verdicts.baseline: A point of reference, not a change
verdicts.kept: The change stayed in the code
verdicts.broken run: The run itself failed; the numbers say nothing about the change
verdicts.unexplained: Numbers not yet trusted; a rerun is due
verdicts.control: The same code with no model, run to show what the model itself added
verdicts.regression: Kept in the code, but it scored worse than what it replaced

experiments.notes: Old corpus of 36 short documents, deleted on 2026-09-11 (#986).

experiments.what: Same as E01 over the whole old corpus.

experiments.label: Blind NuExtract on the six full-page documents

experiments.how: tmp/nuextract-score.ts over the six full-page documents

experiments.label: Old one-shot heuristics
experiments.what: The rules Orbit shipped before ADR-0026: a few regexes per field, first match wins, over the whole page.
experiments.notes: The number every later run is measured against.

experiments.label: Blind NuExtract on the 24
experiments.what: The model read each of the 24 tuning pages whole and wrote every field itself.

experiments.label: First sieve, tag, choose run with the model
experiments.what: ADR-0026 built: stage 1 finds every candidate, stage 2 tags each with the label beside it, stage 3 chooses per field. Rules choose dates, reference, cost; the model chooses provider and subtype from a short list. Subtype truth was still the printed title.
experiments.notes: Subtype negative because the truth convention was wrong, not the chooser.

experiments.label: Subtype means the kind of thing, from the taxonomy
experiments.what: Subtype truth rewritten to a short vocabulary of kinds and qualifiers (subtype-taxonomy.json). The model chooses from the taxonomy phrases the page's words support, about eight a page.

experiments.label: Control: E07's code with no model
experiments.what: E07's pipeline with the chooser switched off, so the rules answer alone. The gap to E07 is what the model itself was worth: provider 45.8 to 75.0 and subtype 0 to 91.7, 15 points of the 80.8 overall.
experiments.how: npm run eval:stages (no --model), re-run 2026-09-12 in a worktree at 12c355b
experiments.notes: Run on 2026-09-12, not on the day of E07.

experiments.label: Old one-shot heuristics, on the hold-out
experiments.what: The rules Orbit shipped before ADR-0026, on the twelve pages nobody tuned on. Every eval prints this line beside its own; it was never written down as a row, so the hold-out table had no 'before' to measure against.
experiments.notes: Unchanged by anything since: the one-shot rules are still in the code as the comparison line.

experiments.label: First hold-out run
experiments.what: E07's pipeline on twelve pages nobody tuned on. The hold-out judges; the 24 only steer.

experiments.label: Control: E08's code with no model
experiments.what: E08 with the chooser switched off. The model's whole contribution was subtype (0 to 66.7); on provider it did worse than the rules, -41.7 against -16.7.
experiments.how: npm run eval:holdout (no --model), re-run 2026-09-12 in a worktree at 5cd5e7e

experiments.label: Date sieves: read every date several ways
experiments.what: Stage 2 reads each date by the label in front, the sentence around it, the heading above and the range it sits in, and keeps the dates no rule could label for the model to pick from.
experiments.notes: Dates 50% to 100% on the hold-out.

experiments.label: Control: E09's code with no model
experiments.what: E09 with the chooser switched off. The date sieves, not the model, are what took dates to 100. Again the model only added subtype and again it lost points on provider.
experiments.how: npm run eval:holdout (no --model), re-run 2026-09-12 in a worktree at 6d71b48

experiments.label: Provider and cost sieves: six and seven ways
experiments.what: Organisations read six ways and amounts seven ways in stage 2; provider answered only where two sieves agree, cost only where the page gave two reasons.

experiments.label: Control: E10's code with no model
experiments.what: E10 with the chooser switched off. Provider is identical with and without the model, -25.0 either way: on this code the model was not deciding provider at all.
experiments.how: npm run eval:holdout (no --model), re-run 2026-09-12 in a worktree at f58701b

experiments.label: Blind NuExtract on the hold-out
experiments.what: The whole-page model, for comparison, on the twelve hold-out pages.
experiments.how: npm run eval:extraction over the hold-out
experiments.notes: Higher than E10 on the hold-out: the whole-page model beats the staged pipeline there on provider and reference.

experiments.label: Model chooses every field; provider ranked by word runs
experiments.what: Every field goes to the model over a ranked short list (rules only rank and fall back). Provider shortlist ranked by the runs of words a page repeats. Run with a chooser setting that had just been removed from the code.
experiments.notes: Recorded as a broken run on the night. E24 reruns the same idea with the same model on healthy code and reproduces the collapse, so this was the design failing, not the run. The two numbers differ (-17.6 against -5.7) because the code moved on between them.

experiments.label: Control: before the word-run bins, rules only
experiments.what: The rules answering alone just before the word-run bins landed. Provider was still being reassembled from the sieve cuts by rules about legal suffixes and how often each cut was printed: 18 of 24 right.
experiments.how: npm run eval:stages (no --model), re-run 2026-09-12 in a worktree at cfab6d6
experiments.notes: The number to judge the provider bins against.

experiments.label: Provider word-run bins rank the shortlist
experiments.what: The owner's method: bin every run of consecutive words across the organisation names stage 2 kept, count how often the page prints each run, and rank the shortlist by that count. The shortlist got better (M03); the rules' own answer was untouched, so the score does not move.
experiments.how: npm run eval:stages (no --model), re-run 2026-09-12 in a worktree at e054ad9
experiments.notes: What this bought is in the shortlist table, not here: it is a ranking change.

experiments.label: The rules answer with the top word run
experiments.what: Nested runs fold into the longer name containing them, and with no model to ask the rules now take the top run outright. Folding fixed the shortlist (23 of 24, top two 22 of 24) but the top run alone is a worse answer than the reassembly rule it replaced: provider 75.0 to 45.8.
experiments.how: npm run eval:stages (no --model), re-run 2026-09-12 in a worktree at eefeb3d
experiments.notes: Still the live behaviour: E15 scores the same provider 45.8. The bins are good at ranking and poor at deciding.

experiments.label: qwen3:4b as the chooser
experiments.what: Same pipeline as E12, questions sent to qwen3:4b over Ollama chat with thinking off.
experiments.notes: Recorded as unexplained on the night. E26 reruns it on healthy code and reproduces the collapse (-10.9%), so it was the design, not the run.

experiments.label: qwen3:4b on the hold-out
experiments.what: E13 on the hold-out.
experiments.notes: Recorded as unexplained on the night. Its tuning-corpus twin (E13) is now reproduced by E26, so this is the same dead end rather than a failed run. Not itself re-run on the hold-out.

experiments.label: Rules only on the hold-out, with subtype from the taxonomy bins
experiments.what: Today's code with no model anywhere. It equals the best model run the hold-out has ever seen (E10, 41.3), and it gets there without asking anything: the taxonomy bins now do the subtype job the model was doing.
experiments.notes: The hold-out's best trusted number, and no model was called.

experiments.label: Rules only, with subtype from the taxonomy bins
experiments.what: No model. Subtype's shortlist is now the two qualifier groups and two kind groups the page's headings and provider names land in most; the rules answer each half where the top group stands clear. Provider answers the top word run where it stands clear.
experiments.notes: Earlier rules-only points from ADR-0026: 75.1% before the model chose every field, 71.5% after provider moved to word runs (per-field split not kept). Subtype 0 to 20/24 is this change.

experiments.label: NuExtract chooses every field, on today's code
experiments.what: The rerun that was meant to tell us whether E12 was a broken run. It was not: asking NuExtract to pick every field off its shortlist reproduces the collapse on healthy code. It answers blank or wrong on dates, roles, cost and provider, and is only better than the rules at subtype (91.7 against 83.3).
experiments.how: npm run eval:stages -- --model, in a node:22 container on the orbit_orbit-document-processing network
experiments.notes: Against E15, the same code with no model: 81.9% to -5.7%. Provider 0.0% means it answered none every time it was asked.

experiments.label: qwen3:4b chooses every field, on today's code
experiments.what: The second half of the rerun: the same questions to qwen3:4b over Ollama chat with thinking off. It reproduces E13, so neither untrusted run was a broken run. qwen is worse than NuExtract at the one field a model was good at: subtype 79.2 against 91.7, and below the rules' own 83.3.
experiments.how: npm run eval:stages -- --model --chooser-model qwen3:4b, in a node:22 container on the orbit_orbit-document-processing network
experiments.notes: Against E15, the same code with no model: 81.9% to -10.9%.

experiments.label: Rules only, scored by right answers
experiments.what: The same code as E15, scored the new way. No model.

experiments.label: Rules only on the unseen twelve, scored by right answers
experiments.what: The same code as E23, scored the new way: 71 of the 109 points the twelve unseen pages want, with no model anywhere.

experiments.label: Old one-shot heuristics, scored by right answers
experiments.what: What Orbit shipped before ADR-0026, on the same twelve, scored the same way. The baseline the staged rules are measured against.

experiments.label: Subtype by describer-word runs, on the unseen twelve
experiments.what: The owner's third method of 2026-09-11, built and measured at last: count the runs of taxonomy words that the headings and the provider organisations repeat, and answer with the first run the taxonomy composes a subtype from. Nine of the twelve right, against ten for the taxonomy bins it was meant to beat.
experiments.notes: One document apart from the bins, which a twelve-page hold-out cannot resolve. The diagnostic the method was written for is the better number: the right answer is in one of its top two runs on 11 of the 12, so it ranks well and picks badly.

experiments.label: Subtype by describer-word runs, on the 24
experiments.what: The same method on the pages the extractor was tuned against: 23 of 24, where the taxonomy bins get 22. It wins here and loses on the unseen twelve, which is the whole reason the hold-out exists.
experiments.notes: The right answer is in its top two runs on all 24.

experiments.label: Provider by the top word run, on the unseen twelve
experiments.what: What the provider word-run bins would answer with if the rules simply took their best run: right on 3 of the 12 unseen pages. The same bins put the right provider in their top two on only 4 of the 12, so the ranking is what fails, not the picking (#994).
experiments.notes: Marked by eye rather than by the scorer the numbers are 5 of 12 top-1 and 8 of 12 top-2, because the bins often answer with a short form of the right name.

experiments.label: Provider by the top word run, on the 24
experiments.what: The same bins on the tuning pages: right on 17 of 24. They rank far better here -- the right provider is in the top two on 22 of the 24 -- which is the split #994 is about.

experiments.label: Provider with its own stage 1 sieve, on the unseen twelve
experiments.what: Provider stops sharing the sieve. Its own first pass cuts every run of capitalised words rather than only names ending in a known trade word, so the right name reaches stage 2 on 11 of 12 unseen pages instead of 5. The whole route then answers right on 6 of 12, against 3 before.
experiments.notes: Marked by eye rather than by classifyProvider it is 10 of 12. Stage 2 and the bins are still the shared ones; only stage 1 changed. Costs 32 candidates a page instead of 11. CONTAMINATED: the hold-out pages' provider answers were read before this sieve was designed (see #996). Not a hold-out number.

experiments.label: Provider with its own stage 1 sieve, on the 24
experiments.what: The same sieve on the pages the extractor was tuned against: recall goes to 24 of 24, but the strict answer falls from 17 to 10. The extra candidates make the top word run a fragment or an over-long phrase that classifyProvider will not accept; marked by eye it is 17 of 24, unchanged.
experiments.notes: Read beside E34. The tuning pages were already well served by the shared sieve, so here the widening only costs; the unseen pages are where it pays. CONTAMINATED: the hold-out pages' provider answers were read before this sieve was designed (see #996). Not a hold-out number.

experiments.label: Rules on the second unseen twelve, every field
experiments.what: The whole rules route on twelve pages nobody had read. Dates hold at 26 of 26; provider 6 of 12; subtype falls to 2 of 12 against 10 of 12 on the first unseen set.
experiments.notes: First and only run on hold-out 2 for this route. Read against E28 (first unseen twelve): dates, cost and scheduleKind hold; subtype and recurrence do not, so the first set was kinder to the subtype rules than the second.

experiments.label: Provider word runs with the joining-word trim, second unseen twelve
experiments.what: Shared stage 1 and 2, word-run bins with runs that start or end on a joining word dropped (3695221). 6 of 12.
experiments.notes: Single run. Same as the plain route (E36 provider) on this set.

experiments.label: Provider's own stage 1 on the second unseen twelve
experiments.what: The honest number for #996. Recall 8 of 12 against the shared sieve's 7; end to end 5 of 12 against the shared sieve's 6, with 19 candidates a page against 8. The gain E34 showed on the first unseen set was fitting to pages whose answers had been read.
experiments.notes: Single run. Marked by eye 6 of 12. Replaces the contaminated E34/E35 as the stage 1 measurement.

experiments.label: Subtype by describer runs, second unseen twelve
experiments.what: Describer-word runs answer 4 of 12 against the taxonomy bins' 2 of 12 on the same pages; in the top two runs 5 of 12.
experiments.notes: Single run. Both subtype methods fall hard from the first unseen set (10 of 12): the subtype rules were closer to the first set's wording than to this one.

measurements.label: Provider shortlist after nested runs fold into the longer name
measurements.what: A run printed exactly as often as a longer run containing it says nothing extra, so it folds away. Before folding, eight shortlist places were going to eight cuts of one name and pushing the answer off the end.

measurements.label: Every shortlist today: can the chooser even see the right answer?
measurements.what: How often the true answer is on the list a chooser is handed, per field, and how long that list is. This is the ceiling on everything the chooser can score.

measurements.label: Provider word-run bins on the twelve unseen pages
measurements.what: The bins were adopted on the strength of the 24. Measured over all twelve unseen pages, they do not carry over: the answer reaches the top two runs a third of the time, against nine times in ten on the 24. Marked generously -- counting a short form of the name as a hit, the way a reader marking by hand would -- it is two thirds. Binning over every organisation stage 1 found, rather than only the ones a provider sieve kept, changes nothing, so the gate in front of the bins is not the cause.

measurements.label: The owner's original method, built and measured against the one that shipped
measurements.what: Two different methods have been called the same thing. The owner's, as they describe it: bin every word across the names the sieve kept, take the top six, then look for places where those words sit next to each other and rank those strings by how often they are printed. What shipped: count every run of consecutive words, whatever the words are worth on their own, and fold a run into the longer name containing it. The single-word bins are computed in the prototype and then thrown away. So no code has ever run the owner's method until now.
